findings.title: CSS compositor pixels advance beyond frozen semantic geometry
findings.failureScenario: A live CSS transform animation moves a 20x20 green button 160px over 1 second while timer and rAF lanes update independently. samplePair reads bounds from the paused source and captures the sole top-level screenshot. The captured button is ahead of the semantic bounds, so controls and saved geometry can target a different location than shown pixels.
findings.oracle: Unchanged production readHtmlSemantics and samplePair. At floor(bounds.x+5), floor(bounds.y+5), exact green is required. Timer/rAF/pending lane values also require exact 8-bit black/white encoding and grayscale channels. No tolerance, sleeps, retries, second screenshot or semantic backfill.
findings.rootCauseStatus: Disabling native threaded CSS animation aligns the source CSS animation clock with the unchanged debugger/global-rate sampling boundary. Original independent128-frame and expanded88-frame exact functional matrices pass, with final source byte-identical to the tested private native main.mm. Source compositor smooth scrolling remains a separate F2 limitation.

findings.title: Feedback-layer pixel test covers source region and one alpha point
findings.fact: The changed test counts and excludes all mismatching channels inside the product feedback rectangle, then compares one composed background pixel. It verifies source channels outside that rectangle and one feedback alpha point. It does not verify the entire feedback rectangle or feedback text pixels.
findings.requiredReporting: Keep any claims scoped accordingly, or extend the expected Canvas to include the exact feedback text/composition and compare all channels. Executor notified.

findings.title: Source compositor smooth scrolling advances while JavaScript semantics are paused
findings.scenario: The original source requests native smooth scrollIntoView for an offscreen label. No test delay is inserted before production sampling. The JavaScript source and semantics pause at scrollY10 while native scrolling continues to change the root screenshot. Pixel state, metadata scroll and control bounds diverge.

findings.title: Stale semantic selection application echoes a new accepted input that overwrites user selection
findings.source: src/web/html-surface/Controls.tsx TextProxy selection effect and src/web/html-surface/InputProxy.ts select listener
findings.failureScenario: A newer user selection0..2 is pending/accepted while frame12 still represents inputSeq53 with old selection5..5. TextProxy unconditionally applies that stale source selection; the select listener sends it as a new text-selection inputSeq55, replacing the user-owned selection.
findings.correctionBoundary: Local unconfirmed selection must keep ownership until a semantic frame covers the accepted input. Applying source state must not become a new user selection operation. Executor owns implementation; reviewer source untouched.
findings.scope: Original input/IME acceptance. Independent of F2 native scrolling and distinct from a test that sends IME before selection acknowledgement.
